# Cache penetration results

These are deterministic observations for two nonexistent-key request distributions. Origin work is modeled from lookup counts rather than measured against a database.

## Environment

- Date: 2026-09-02
- Host: Apple M4, 10 logical CPUs
- OS: macOS 26.5.1, Darwin arm64
- Go: 1.26.6
- Command: `go run .`

## Experiment Variables

- Valid keys represented by each Bloom Filter: 100,000
- Requests per workload: 10,000
- Distinct nonexistent keys in repeated workload: 100
- Distinct nonexistent keys in unique workload: 10,000
- Assumed origin cost: 5 ms per lookup

## Results

| Workload | Strategy | Origin calls | Avoided origin | Bloom false positives | Negative hits | Negative entries | Bloom memory | Modeled origin work |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| repeated | none | 10000 | 0.00% | - | 0 | 0 | - | 50s |
| repeated | negative | 100 | 99.00% | - | 9900 | 100 | - | 500ms |
| repeated | bloom-4 | 1400 | 86.00% | 14.00% | 0 | 0 | 48.8 KiB | 7s |
| repeated | bloom-8 | 100 | 99.00% | 1.00% | 0 | 0 | 97.7 KiB | 500ms |
| repeated | bloom-12 | 0 | 100.00% | 0.00% | 0 | 0 | 146.5 KiB | 0s |
| repeated | bloom-8+negative | 1 | 99.99% | 1.00% | 99 | 1 | 97.7 KiB | 5ms |
| unique | none | 10000 | 0.00% | - | 0 | 0 | - | 50s |
| unique | negative | 10000 | 0.00% | - | 0 | 10000 | - | 50s |
| unique | bloom-4 | 1445 | 85.55% | 14.45% | 0 | 0 | 48.8 KiB | 7.225s |
| unique | bloom-8 | 205 | 97.95% | 2.05% | 0 | 0 | 97.7 KiB | 1.025s |
| unique | bloom-12 | 32 | 99.68% | 0.32% | 0 | 0 | 146.5 KiB | 160ms |
| unique | bloom-8+negative | 205 | 97.95% | 2.05% | 0 | 205 | 97.7 KiB | 1.025s |

## Observations

Negative caching was effective when keys repeated: 100 first lookups created 100 markers, and those markers absorbed the remaining 9,900 requests. With 10,000 unique keys, it avoided no origin work and retained 10,000 markers that were never reused.

For unique missing keys, observed Bloom false-positive rates were 14.45%, 2.05%, and 0.32% at 4, 8, and 12 bits per valid item. The corresponding bit arrays used 48.8 KiB, 97.7 KiB, and 146.5 KiB. These observations closely followed the expected memory-probability tradeoff for this deterministic hash distribution.

The repeated workload sampled only 100 distinct filter outcomes. At 8 bits per item, one of those 100 missing keys was a false positive, so its 100 repeated requests all reached the origin with Bloom alone. Adding negative caching reduced those 100 requests to one origin lookup plus 99 negative hits.

None of the 100 repeated missing keys was a false positive in the 12-bit filter. This finite `0.00%` observation does not mean a 12-bit filter has zero theoretical false positives; the 10,000-key unique workload observed 32.

## Caveats

- The experiment does not execute the modeled 5 ms origin work, so the work column is arithmetic rather than wall-clock timing.
- Every request is for missing data. Existing-key cache behavior and Bloom lookup CPU cost are outside this result.
- Negative markers do not expire during the finite run, and logical entry counts omit actual map and metadata overhead.
- Bloom filters are populated once from a fixed valid set. Update lag and rebuild cost are not represented.
- Different key distributions and hash functions can change observed finite-sample false-positive rates.
